title: Full-Stack Modern React and Next.js Application Development
description: Build Field Notes through 20 book-aligned chapters: REST, MongoDB, React, Docker, JWT, server rendering, SEO, tests, analytics, GraphQL, realtime events, and Next.js. Original tutorials, runnable project code, browser practice, and a capstone conclusion.
prerequisites: Use an editor and navigate a folder
learningOutcomes: Build and test a private note workflow across UI, API, and owner-scoped storage
Model asynchronous data, GraphQL mutations, and realtime replay with explicit failure states
Choose React and Next.js boundaries, metadata, and caching policies
Validate inputs, authorization, privacy, accessibility, and release gates with evidence
accessibilityNotes: Text-first chapters and native progressive hints
Keyboard controls with visible focus and readable code blocks
Decorative sky has pause/resume and reduced-motion static behavior
No exact location or public profile is required
Project exercises require keyboard and narrow-screen checks

chapters.title: Preparing for Full-Stack Development
chapters.summary: Set up an editor, Node.js, Git, and the original Field Notes project; make and verify a first React change.
objectives: Distinguish browser, server, and storage responsibilities
Install and run the four-workspace project
Change a React heading and verify a production build

chapters.title: Getting to Know Node.js and MongoDB
chapters.summary: Explore Node I/O, HTTP responses, document modeling, containers, and an optional MongoDB replica set.
objectives: Compare Node and browser capabilities
Explain asynchronous I/O and document query order
Test memory lifetimes and optional Mongo persistence

chapters.title: Implementing a Backend Using Express, Mongoose ODM, and Jest
chapters.summary: Build and test REST routes, schemas, service boundaries, and failure responses.
objectives: Trace an Express request through validation and storage
Define HTTP success and failure contracts
Write Jest/Supertest cases for rejected writes

chapters.title: Integrating a Frontend Using React and TanStack Query
chapters.summary: Connect React components, query identity, loading states, mutations, filtering, and sorting.
objectives: Separate form state from server state
Use query identity and mutation invalidation
Add labeled search and sort controls

chapters.title: Deploying the Application with Docker and CI/CD
chapters.summary: Package the API, understand Compose and registry boundaries, and create a tested release workflow.
objectives: Distinguish images, containers, volumes, registries, and hosts
Build a credential-free API image
Design checks and approval before deployment

chapters.title: Adding Authentication with JWT
chapters.summary: Implement signup, login, password hashing, constrained JWT verification, and ownership checks.
objectives: Explain hashing, signed claims, authentication, and authorization
Verify JWT algorithm, issuer, audience, and expiry
Prove another actor cannot modify a note

chapters.title: Improving the Load Time Using Server-Side Rendering
chapters.summary: Inspect actual initial HTML, server-side data fetching, safe serialization, and hydration.
objectives: Inspect content in initial HTML
Trace safe data serialization and hydration
Compare rendering behavior and measure its limits

chapters.title: Making Sure Customers Find You with Search Engine Optimization
chapters.summary: Create meaningful URLs, titles, canonical metadata, robots rules, sitemaps, and social previews.
objectives: Design meaningful slugs and trusted canonical URLs
Inspect title, social, robots, and sitemap metadata
Separate public discovery from authorization

chapters.title: Implementing End-to-End Tests Using Playwright
chapters.summary: Test a real browser journey with isolated fixtures, semantic locators, failure assertions, and evidence.
objectives: Write role-based browser interactions
Isolate synthetic test accounts and datasets
Assert a rejected record remains absent

chapters.title: Aggregating and Visualizing Statistics Using MongoDB and Victory
chapters.summary: Aggregate note counts, handle UTC grouping, and render a chart with a table alternative.
objectives: Define count units and UTC date groups
Trace a Mongo aggregation pipeline
Render equivalent chart and table values

chapters.title: Building a Backend with a GraphQL API
chapters.summary: Define and execute typed GraphQL queries and authenticated mutations with workload bounds.
objectives: Define GraphQL fields and resolver context
Execute named queries and authenticated mutations
Explain workload bounds and authorization limits

chapters.title: Interfacing with GraphQL on the Frontend Using Apollo Client
chapters.summary: Integrate Apollo queries, mutation variables, cache identity, loading, and error recovery.
objectives: Configure Apollo providers and React hooks
Handle loading, errors, and empty results
Refresh a mutation result and clear caches on logout

chapters.title: Building an Event-Based Backend Using Express and Socket.IO
chapters.summary: Authenticate socket connections and acknowledge only committed, validated events.
objectives: Authenticate Socket.IO connections
Derive room identity on the server
Acknowledge only committed idempotent work

chapters.title: Creating a Frontend to Consume and Send Events
chapters.summary: Connect a React realtime view, clean up listeners, reconcile history, and explain disconnects.
objectives: Manage socket effects and cleanup
Merge live and history events by stable identity
Explain disconnected, pending, and confirmed states

chapters.title: Adding Persistence to Socket.IO Using MongoDB
chapters.summary: Persist events transactionally, scope idempotency, and replay with a bounded cursor.
objectives: Persist note and event in a Mongo transaction
Scope idempotency by author and client ID
Replay author-scoped history using bounded cursors

chapters.title: Getting Started with Next.js
chapters.summary: Use App Router pages, layouts, dynamic routes, metadata, and route handlers.
objectives: Use App Router pages, layouts, and dynamic params
Handle loading, errors, and missing records
Build and start the Next application

chapters.title: Introducing React Server Components
chapters.summary: Separate server data access, interactive client code, serializable props, and authenticated server actions.
objectives: Separate server data work from client interaction
Send only serializable public props
Validate actions and forward credentials server-side

chapters.title: Advanced Next.js Concepts and Optimizations
chapters.summary: Choose explicit cache lifetimes, narrow client boundaries, asset behavior, and observable performance budgets.
objectives: Define explicit cache identity and lifetime
Inspect asset dimensions and client boundaries
Measure a reproducible performance budget

chapters.title: Deploying a Next.js App
chapters.summary: Build, configure, release, smoke-test, and roll back a Next frontend with a separate durable API.
objectives: Configure separate frontend, API, and storage hosts
Verify a production artifact through its public domain
Record smoke checks and a tested rollback target

chapters.title: Diving Deeper into Full-Stack Development
chapters.summary: Complete the Field Notes capstone, review evidence, and choose a next area of deliberate practice.
objectives: Demonstrate the complete notebook lifecycle
Collect negative, accessibility, and release evidence
Write a retrospective and choose one next improvement

completion.rule: Read all chapters and pass their browser checkpoints; collect separate capstone project evidence for human review.
